item.title: Myanmar's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The International Court of Justice has found Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya, prompting the General Assembly President to assure refugees they will not be alone and leading the UK to sanction top Myanmar military leaders. In May 2026 a Burma Army air strike in Doo Tha Htoo District killed one villager, injured five including two children, and destroyed houses in Bilin Township. The junta continues large-scale attacks on Rohingya civilians, destroying bridges in Arakan and extending a 108‑kilometre fence on the Bangladesh border, while admitting corruption in its conscription system and targeting nearly two hundred officials. There were 2,332 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Machine-written from the linked sources, checked for figures and names not in them.
